sections.heading: Verizon: the challenge and our approach
sections.text:
Verizon partnered with Nagarro to create an award winning, best-in-class Digital Signage management platform that combines its powerful plug-and-play hardware (LTE media player), with an intuitive and secure cloud-based content management portal.
Our product and strategy leads, senior engineers  and designers organized workshops with key stakeholders from the Verizon team to define the core workflows and features for this product.  In order to achieve rapid development and testing, we prioritized modules by usage and customer engagement value. This approach was instrumental for rapid development and testing before expanding to other features.

sections.heading: Verizon: scope of work
sections.text:
Discovery: Workshops  Research  Project Planning
Strategy: Stakeholder Alignment Information Architecture Product Roadmapping  Product Ideation User Experience
Design: Prototyping UI Design UX Design  Iconography
Quality Assurance: Performance Testing Functionality Testing
Engineering: Frontend Development Backend Development Android Development

sections.heading: Verizon: guiding product vision
sections.text:
During the 4 year engagement, our role expanded from being one of five dedicated vendors, to leading the project.  Nagarro became the sole trusted provider for related future products.
What we did
Extensive market research of existing products to discover client needs and improve customer retention.
Roadmapping advanced features to gain new clients.
Close collaboration with internal teams, streamlining the process and optimizing resources.
Guided product vision with POC’s (e.g., gaze detection, interactive kiosks, ad platform).
Supported the product team in ideating new product ideas.
Built the Digital Signage Frontend - React web app for managing screens, uploading content to CMS, creating and deploying campaigns.

sections.heading: Verizon: design language
sections.text: We focused on crafting a design language that promotes user engagement with the workflows and content. By implementing a scalable card-based system where users can manage visually rich content (images, videos, graphic templates) seamlessly, we built a product that can extend itself to scale as it continues to grow and evolve.  We built a sophisticated UX and design system that can scale to future needs while allowing Verizon to continue adding more features and empowering its customer base.

sections.heading: Verizon: results
sections.text:
The end result was a solid product with unique functionalities in the market such as minimal need for configuration (self-contained hardware and software package), centralized control prepared for easy large-scale deployment, and the ability to mix corporate and local content across devices. We nourished a trust based relationship with our client, and were able to collaborate on many more projects with Verizon beyond the Digital Signage scope.
Awards: Frost & Sullivan's 2020 Best Practices Award
+17% increase in sales · 30% more views · 48% effectiveness on brand awareness · 500+ clients actively using Verizon Digital Signage

sections.heading: Datto: the challenge
sections.text:
Datto is one of the world's leading cybersecurity and cloud-based company that creates innovative technology providing different solutions and products for its clients. Until now, all the integrations that Datto provides were treated individually. This is specially frustrating since these lines of products are pretty complex and require several people to manage.
Nagarro partnered with Datto to create a platform that centralizes and manages all their applications into one ecosystem. Nagarro also developed a scalable design system to streamline their design process and promote consistency across their products and their new holder company Kaseya.

sections.heading: Datto: collaboration and governance
sections.text:
With Datto’s management change, it was necessary to adapt the current visual identity system for its new and larger family, Kaseya. This means that we had to adapt to a more extensive scope when the merger between the two companies happened. This means that, at this point, we needed to revisit some of the previous work done and put a lot of effort into doing new audits, updating, and changing what we already did to meet the new reality.
Managing expectations and ensuring everyone was on the same page was challenging. A lot of effort was placed into communication — all the teams had shared channels and regular check-in meetings to keep each other updated. Regarding technical tools, we used Figma to create UI and the Design System, Zeroheight for documentation, and dev hand-off
Our governance model in place and a specialized team for the design system allowed us to move much faster and dedicate more time to the experience and interactions of the platform.

sections.heading: Datto: documentation and handover
sections.text:
We ensured we designed a project to last. We supported the client to continue making iterations on the design and keep creating by themselves. We documented all design patterns, development guidelines, product behaviors, and interactions.
Our handoff included instructions on how to use the tools effectively, the organization of the design system, rules in place to keep consistency in the design, the purpose of specific components, etc. We complemented the handoff with video tutorials showing for the users that are not accustomed to the software.

sections.heading: Datto: foundation of the new design language
sections.text:
Datto’s Design System was developed with Datto’s and Kaseya’s design teams while Nagarro created the Datto’s platform at the same time.
Libraries: Components (building blocks of all digital products) · Typography · Colors light theme · Colors dark theme · Layouts and grid · Icons

sections.heading: Datto: scalable and adaptable components
sections.text: We worked with Datto to ensure each component worked and behaved as intended. With a large inventory of components and various applications, we created components that could be easily resized and applicable to other contexts and platforms. Our goal was to design pixel-perfect and straightforward components that enabled Datto to focus on designing the product experience rather than worrying about spacing, color, or type values.

sections.heading: Datto: summing it up
sections.text:
After 6 months, we developed an efficient platform that brought together multiple products under an umbrella and a design system to keep all customer experiences consistent during the acquisition of the company and ready to scale for future growth.
The final product saved resources for the company, making it easier to implement new product lines and more efficient for cooperation between development and design.
